injuries.shortComment: Armstrong caught his only target for a 43-yard touchdown in Sunday's 35-13 win over the Falcons.
injuries.longComment: The wideout played just 17 of 64 offensive snaps against Atlanta and ran only seven pass routes on Patrick Mahomes' 38 dropbacks. Armstrong was tasked with blocking duties on 10 of his snaps. He still managed to catch his first career touchdown in the fourth quarter with the game already well out of hand. Armstrong is not on the fantasy radar.

injuries.shortComment: Allen caught two of four targets for 44 yards and a touchdown in Sunday's 35-13 win over the Falcons.
injuries.longComment: The rookie wideout scored his first career touchdown by beating the cornerback on a stutter-go for a 39-yard touchdown in the third quarter. With Josh Downs still getting comfortable and learning the offense following Tuesday's acquisition from the Colts, Allen maintained a significant role on offense, playing 22 of 64 offensive snaps. Once Downs progresses from the 10 snaps he played against Atlanta, it will be interesting to see if Allen can push Xavier Worthy (zero catches on three targets across 56 snaps on Sunday) for a larger piece of the outside receiver role in Kansas City's offense.

injuries.shortComment: Worthy failed to catch any of his three targets in Sunday's 35-13 win over the Falcons.
injuries.longComment: Worthy ran a team-high 37 routes on Patrick Mahomes' 38 dropbacks, but on a day Mahomes targeted nine different players, Worthy was the only one to not record a catch. With Josh Downs now in the fold and working to get comfortable in the offense, Worthy's role will likely only continue to shrink. On just eight routes in his team debut Sunday, Downs posted a 4-53-1 receiving line on five targets. Worthy hasn't produced that many fantasy points in a game all season. He's waiver-wire fodder in 12-team redraft leagues.

injuries.shortComment: Kelce secured both targets for 30 yards in the Chiefs' 35-13 win over the Falcons on Sunday.
injuries.longComment: Kelce recorded a 23-yard catch on the Chiefs' first play from scrimmage, seemingly a harbinger of a productive day. However, the veteran tight end also suffered an ankle injury on the tackle, and although he was able to return to the game, he had only one more reception the rest of the way. Despite the modest numbers, Kelce managed to keep his season-long streak of games with multiple receptions going, and he's averaging a career-best 14.6  per catch heading into a Week 11 home matchup against the Cardinals next Sunday.

injuries.shortComment: Downs secured four of five targets for 53 yards and a touchdown, fumbled once but recovered and returned three punts for 10 yards in the Chiefs' 35-13 win over the Falcons on Sunday.
injuries.longComment: Making his Chiefs debut following three days of practice after arriving via trade from the Colts on Tuesday, Downs looked right at home in the Patrick Mahomes-led offense. The young wideout fully capitalized on the upgrade he saw at quarterback, finishing third in receptions, receiving yards and targets right out of the gate and adding his second touchdown of the season on a difficult 18-yard catch just before halftime. Downs' immediate chemistry with Mahomes is highly welcome news for fantasy managers, and he'll aim to carry the momentum over into a favorable Week 11 home matchup against the Cardinals next Sunday.

injuries.shortComment: Johnson rushed 22 times for 101 yards and brought in six of seven targets for 70 yards and two touchdowns in the Chiefs' 35-13 win over the Falcons on Sunday.
injuries.longComment: Drawing his first career start due to Kenneth Walker (groin) being sidelined, Johnson put on a pretty convincing impression of his star teammate. Not only did Johnson just get himself over the century mark in rushing yards, but he finished as the team leader in receptions and targets while checking in as the runner-up in receiving yards. Johnson struck from 12 and six yards out for his two receiving TDs, underscoring his considerable versatility. If Walker is unable to garner active status for next Sunday's Week 11 matchup against the Cardinals, the Chiefs' ground attack will remain in good hands with Johnson.

injuries.shortComment: Rice brought in five of six targets for 82 yards in the Chiefs' 35-13 win over the Falcons on Sunday.
injuries.longComment: Rice led the Chiefs in receiving yards and finished second in receptions and targets on a prolific afternoon for the Chiefs' air attack. Rice didn't get in on the scoring fun of a five-touchdown day for Patrick Mahomes, but he still eclipsed 80 receiving yards for the third time this season and first time since Week 3. Rice's level of involvement was encouraging given the debuting Josh Downs drew five targets, keeping the former's prospects bright for a favorable Week 11 home matchup against the Cardinals next Sunday.

injuries.shortComment: Mahomes completed 22 of 35 passes for 348 yards with five touchdowns and no interceptions while adding two rushes for 15 yards in the Chiefs' 35-13 win over the Falcons on Sunday.
injuries.longComment: Taking advantage of a controlled environment and a fast track at Mercedes-Benz Stadium -- not to mention the presence of the debuting Josh Downs -- Mahomes repeatedly exploited the vulnerabilities of the Falcons defense throughout the afternoon. The legendary signal-caller showed no ill effects from the elbow injury that he'd suffered in Week 9, and he connected with Emmett Johnson (12, six yards), Downs (18 yards), Cyrus Allen (39 yards) and Andrew Armstrong (43 yards) for his quintet of touchdown passes. Mahomes now has multiple scoring strikes and zero interceptions in three straight games, and Sunday's five TD tosses represented a new season high. Mahomes will take 2,385 passing yards and a 19:4 TD:INT into a Week 11 home matchup against the Cardinals next Sunday.

injuries.shortComment: Wiley suffered a fractured ankle in the Chiefs' 35-13 victory over the Falcons on Sunday, Matt Derrick of ChiefsDigest.com reports.
injuries.longComment: Wiley was carted to the locker room in the first quarter with an ankle injury. The tight end fractured his ankle and did not return to the contest. The 26-year-old will likely be placed on injured reserve soon, as he begins to recover from the injury.

injuries.shortComment: Smith (concussion) has been ruled out for the remainder of Sunday's game against the Falcons.
injuries.longComment: Smith has entered the NFL's five-step concussion protocol and will not return to Sunday's game. Mike Caliendo is set to finish the game at right guard.

injuries.shortComment: Delane (shoulder) is active for Sunday's game against the Falcons, Matt McMullen of the Chiefs' official site reports.
injuries.longComment: Delane has been given the green light to return from a two-game absence due to a shoulder injury. The rookie first-rounder will likely return to his starting role at outside cornerback opposite Nohl Williams, while Kristian Fulton and Christian Roland-Wallace provide depth at the position.

injuries.shortComment: Jones recorded four tackles (two solo), including 2.0 sacks, and a pass breakup in Sunday's 35-12 win over the Jets.
injuries.longComment: The 32-year-old defensive lineman had gotten off to a slow start to begin the 2026 season, his 11th in the league. Prior to Sunday, he'd recorded just 0.5 sacks across the first seven games, so his 2.0 sacks were his first full ones of the campaign. Jones is now up to 17 tackles (eight solo), including 2.5 sacks, three pass breakups and a fumble recovery on 72 percent of the defensive snaps.

injuries.shortComment: Karlaftis recorded six tackles (four solo), including 2.0 sacks, and a pass breakup in Sunday's 35-12 win over the Jets.
injuries.longComment: After starting the season without a sack in his first four games, Karlaftis has 4.0 sacks over his last four contests. For the season, the 25-year-old edge rusher is up to 32 tackles (16 solo), including the 4.0 sacks, a career-high nine pass breakups, including his first career interception, and a forced fumble across eight games. He's on pace to shatter his previous career high of 48 tackles, which was set last season.

injuries.shortComment: Bolton recorded 12 tackles (five solo) and a forced fumble in Sunday's 35-12 win over the Jets.
injuries.longComment: Bolton doesn't do much in the box scores other than rack up tackles, but he's good at that and now has five double-digit tackles games through eight contests to begin the 2026 campaign. For the season, Bolton is up to 80 tackles (39 solo), two pass breakups and a forced fumble on 99 percent of the Chiefs' defensive snaps.

injuries.shortComment: Tranquill collected 13 tackles (seven solo) in Sunday's 35-12 win over the Jets.
injuries.longComment: It was Tranquill's second double-digit tackles game of the season, and both have come over the last three weeks. The veteran linebacker has piled up 66 tackles (33 solo), two pass breakups and one fumble recovery on 88 percent of the defensive snaps across eight games this season.

injuries.shortComment: Fields carried twice for minus-one yard and lost a fumble while logging five snaps on offense in Sunday's 35-12 win over the Jets.
injuries.longComment: The Chiefs' backup quarterback saw the field for just the second time this season, after he had previously played one snap in a Week 1 win over the Broncos. Due to head coach Andy Reid's reluctance to use starter Patrick Mahomes on quarterback sneaks, Fields subbed into the game for a third-and-1 play in the first quarter. Fields ended up coughing the football, with the Jets making the recovery. The Chiefs went on to build enough of a lead to rest Mahomes for the final possession of the game with just over two minutes left in the fourth quarter, when Fields proceeded to hand the ball off three times before kneeling to run out the clock.

injuries.shortComment: Gay went 2-for-2 on field-goal tries and made his only PAT during Sunday's 21-13 loss to the Seahawks.
injuries.longComment: Gay was able to convert multiple field goals for the sixth time this season and first time since Week 7. The kicker has now gone 21-for-23 on field-goal attempts, including 3-for-4 from 50-plus yards, while making all 22 of his extra-point tries over 10 contests so far this season.

injuries.shortComment: Young went without a target while playing one of the Raiders' 59 snaps on offense in Sunday's 21-13 loss to the Seahawks. He also brought back one kickoff for 29 yards.
injuries.longComment: Young has suited up in each of the Raiders' 10 games this season, but he's been deployed almost exclusively on special teams. He's seen single-digit snaps on offense in five straight games and has posted a collective 2-36-0 receiving line on three targets on the campaign.

injuries.shortComment: Raiders head coach Klint Kubiak confirmed Monday that Bowers (ankle) is considered day-to-day after exiting Sunday's 21-13 loss to the Seahawks, Sam Warren of The Athletic reports. "It's not as bad as we thought, but still a significant injury," Kubiak said.
injuries.longComment: Bowers checked in and out of Sunday's contest as he managed the ankle issue, finishing with two catches for 18 yards on two targets while logging just 11 snaps on offense. Per Ryan McFadden of ESPN.com, Kubiak added that Bowers will continue to be evaluated throughout the week as the Raiders look to determine whether the star tight end will be available for next Sunday's game in Denver. If Bowers is forced to miss his third game of the season, the Raiders would have more targets up for grabs for the likes of tight end Michael Mayer, running back Ashton Jeanty and wideouts Tre Tucker, Jalen Nailor and Jack Bech.

injuries.shortComment: Nailor recorded one reception for minus-1 yard on four targets in Sunday's 21-13 loss to the Seahawks.
injuries.longComment: Making his first NFL start, No. 1 overall pick Fernando Mendoza was under siege throughout the afternoon, as a ferocious Seahawks defense sacked him six times and limited him to just 143 passing yards on 29 attempts. As a result, Nailor and the Raiders' other pass catchers were held quiet, with running back Ashton Jeanty (four receptions for 46 yards) being the only Las Vegas player to top two catches and 25 receiving yards. Though Mendoza will get some more favorable matchups over the Raiders' final seven games, Nailor will be difficult to count on for production. Even while Kirk Cousins served as the starting quarterback for Las Vegas before being traded to the Vikings last week, Nailor was limited to just 14 receptions for 122 yards and one touchdown on 28 targets through eight appearances.

injuries.shortComment: Laube played all 22 of his snaps on special teams in Sunday's 21-13 loss to the Seahawks and returned two kickoffs for 46 yards and one punt for zero yards.
injuries.longComment: Since earning seven touches in a Week 5 blowout loss to the Patriots, Laube has been an afterthought on offense. He's played just eight total offense snaps in the Raiders' ensuing five games, and Sunday marked the first time all season that he was limited exclusively to special teams.

injuries.shortComment: Mayer caught two of three targets for 16 yards in Sunday's 21-13 loss to the Seahawks.
injuries.longComment: Jack Bech (seven targets) was the only Las Vegas player to see more than four targets in Fernando Mendoza's first career start. The rookie quarterback targeted 10 different players on his 29 attempts. With Kirk Cousins' efficiency off to Minnesota, Mayer is a low-floor TE2 for fantasy, but he could get a bit of a boost if Brock Bowers' ankle injury causes him to miss time.

injuries.shortComment: Tucker caught one pass for nine yards on two targets in Sunday's 21-13 loss to the Seahawks.
injuries.longComment: In Fernando Mendoza's first career start at quarterback, Tucker saw just 6.9 percent of the targets, while Jack Bech led the team with seven looks. Tucker looks like someone who won't be usable in fantasy until he shows some tangible chemistry with the young quarterback.

injuries.shortComment: Mendoza completed 17 of 29 passes for 143 yards, no touchdowns and no interceptions and rushed six times for 22 yards and one TD during Sunday's 21-13 loss to the Seahawks.
injuries.longComment: The Mendoza era in Las Vegas officially kicked off this week following the trade of veteran QB Kirk Cousins to the Vikings, and the rookie first overall pick unsurprisingly flashed at times while also stalling numerous drives by taking six sacks overall. On a positive note, Mendoza didn't turn the ball over, and he also recorded his first touchdown as a pro on a 10-yard run on the Raiders' opening offensive possession. He'll seek to build on the initial start of his career next Sunday at Denver.

injuries.shortComment: Washington compiled eight rushes for 23 yards and secured his only target for four yards during Sunday's 21-13 defeat to the Seahawks.
injuries.longComment: Aside from a 25-carry outburst in Week 8 at the Jets, Washington has logged 54 rushes along with four catches in nine appearances, which amounts to 6.4 touches per game. Despite that number, he continues to eat into the overall backfield picture, as lead runner Ashton Jeanty failed to tally double-digit rushes for a fourth straight contest Sunday. Washington should retain a modest role alongside Jeanty next Sunday at Denver.

injuries.shortComment: Jeanty turned his nine carries into just 18 yards and caught all four of his targets for 46 yards during Sunday's 21-13 loss to the Seahawks.
injuries.longComment: After reaching the 10-carry threshold in each of the first six games of the season, Jeanty has failed to do so in four straight contests, and he also has fallen shy of 30 rushing yards in six consecutive outings. Rookie RB Mike Washington continued to split the backfield with Jeanty in Week 10, turning his nine touches into 27 yards from scrimmage. Considering recent trends, Jeanty is difficult to trust for consistent production without a boost in work.

injuries.shortComment: Paye (neck) is questionable to return to Sunday's game against the Seahawks.
injuries.longComment: Paye exited the second half of Sunday's game with a neck injury. The linebacker logged five tackles before departing. Malcolm Koonce will likely finish the game at strongside linebacker opposite Maxx Crosby.

injuries.shortComment: Benson (coach's decision) is inactive for Sunday's game against the Seahawks.
injuries.longComment: Benson is a healthy scratch for a third consecutive week. The rookie sixth-rounder has failed to find a place in a wide-open receiving corps so far, and it remains to be seen how coach Klint Kubiak will utilize him.

injuries.shortComment: Booker (ankle) is inactive for Sunday's game against the Seahawks.
injuries.longComment: Booker was a full participant in Friday's practice but remained questionable headed into the weekend. The defensive lineman appears to not be quite ready to suit up, leaving JJ Pegues to see more defensive snaps in Sunday's contest.

injuries.shortComment: Thornton (back) is inactive for Sunday's game against the Seahawks.
injuries.longComment: Thornton was a late addition to the Raiders' injury report due to a back issue. It's been determined by medical staff that the second-year wide receiver will not play in Sunday's contest, and Thornton has yet to play in a regular-season game in 2026 after appearing in 15 contests during his rookie campaign. Dareke Young and Cody White will operate as the depth options at wide receiver behind Tre Tucker, Jalen Nailor and Jack Bech.

injuries.shortComment: Zuhn (concussion) does not have any injury designation ahead of Sunday's game against the Seahawks, Ryan McFadden of ESPN.com reports.
injuries.longComment: Zuhn started Week 10 prep with a pair of limited practices before upgrading to full participation in Friday's session. The starting left guard has cleared the NFL's five-step concussion protocol and is all set to suit up for Sunday's game against the defending champion Seahawks.

injuries.shortComment: Fatukasi (shoulder/back) was a full participant at practice Thursday, John Boyle of the Seahawks' official site reports.
injuries.longComment: Fatukasi popped up on the Raiders' injury report Wednesday with shoulder and back issues, but it seems like those were minor, and he's in line to suit up in Week 10. He figures to start on the defensive line Sunday versus the Seahawks.

injuries.shortComment: Stukes registered five tackles (three solo) and an interception during the Raiders' 38-17 loss to the 49ers in Week 9.
injuries.longComment: Stukes jumped in front of a Brock Purdy pass intended for George Kittle midway through the third quarter, although the Raiders' offense gave the ball right back to the 49ers two plays later on a Brock Bowers fumble. It was the second interception of the season for Stukes, who was a second-round selection of the Raiders in the 2026 NFL Draft. The rookie out of Arizona is up to 43 tackles (23 solo) and four pass defenses through the first eight regular-season games of his NFL career.

injuries.shortComment: Chinn recorded nine tackles (six solo) during the Raiders' 38-17 loss to the 49ers in Week 9.
injuries.longComment: Chinn finished Week 9 as the Raiders' third-leading tackler behind Nakobe Dean (19) and Quay Walker (11). Dean has logged at least seven stops in five consecutive outings, and he has accumulated 66 tackles (44 solo), including 1.0 sacks, two pass defenses (including one interception), two forced fumbles and two fumble recoveries over nine regular-season games.

injuries.shortComment: Walker posted 11 tackles (three solo) during the Raiders' 38-17 loss to the 49ers in Week 9.
injuries.longComment: It was the second time in three games that Walker finished with double-digit stops, and he finished second on the Raiders in tackles behind Nakobe Dean (19). Walker is on track for his fifth consecutive 100-plus tackle campaign and is up to 72 stops (28 solo), including 2.0 sacks, and one fumble recovery through nine regular-season games.

injuries.shortComment: Dean logged 19 tackles (seven solo) during the Raiders' 38-17 loss to the 49ers in Week 9.
injuries.longComment: Dean played every defensive snap and was all over the field in Week 9, finishing with a career-best 19 total tackles. He's logged at least 12 tackles in six of his last seven outings, and through nine regular-season games he has accumulated 98 total tackles, which is second-most in the NFL behind Alex Singleton (107).

injuries.shortComment: O'Connell moves to QB No. 2 on the depth chart behind Fernando Mendoza, Sam Warren of The Athletic reports.
injuries.longComment: O'Connell is set to back up rookie Mendoza, who replaced recently traded Kirk Cousins as the starting quarterback. O'Connell has been with Las Vegas since the team drafted him in the fourth round of the 2023 NFL Draft. The 28-year-old last appeared in a regular-season game in 2025, completing 10 of 22 attempts for 102 yards.

injuries.shortComment: Bech caught one of two targets for nine yards Sunday in a loss to the 49ers.
injuries.longComment: Bech logged a 34 percent offensive snap share, third-highest among Raiders wideouts behind Jalen Nailor (74 percent) and Tre Tucker (64 percent). Though he seems fairly secure in the No. 3 wideout role, Bech hasn't done much this season, producing no more than three catches or 25 yards in any of his five games to date.

injuries.shortComment: Shelley (ankle) is questionable to return to Monday night's contest against the Ravens, Noah Furtado of The Athletic reports.
injuries.longComment: Shelley is dealing with an apparent ankle injury, and his status for the remainder of the second half is now uncertain. In his absence, Deane Leonard is a top candidate to see an increase in workload in the secondary with Los Angeles.

injuries.shortComment: Gadsden (eye) returned to Monday night's game against the Ravens, Noah Furtado of The Athletic reports.
injuries.longComment: Gadsden was poked in the eye in the first quarter and had to go to the locker room before returning early in the second quarter. He wasn't targeted in the passing game prior to sustaining the injury.

injuries.shortComment: Thompson (hamstring) is inactive for Monday night's game against the Ravens.
injuries.longComment: Thompson will not suit up for Monday's primetime clash. The wide receiver was listed as doubtful after Friday's third consecutive DNP, and it is no surprise that the fourth-round rookie is unable to play in Monday's game. Derius Davis will take on the role of No. 4 wide receiver in the contest behind starters Quentin Johnston, Tre' Harris and KeAndre Lambert-Smith.

injuries.shortComment: Awosika (fibula) is active for Monday's game against the Ravens.
injuries.longComment: Awosika will suit up Monday for the first time since Week 2, when he suffered an injury to his fibula. He should slide back into his starting role at left guard.

injuries.shortComment: Eboigbe (ankle) is inactive for Monday's game against the Ravens, Omar Navarro of the Chargers' official site reports.
injuries.longComment: Eboigbe suffered an ankle injury against the Texans in Week 9, and he will be sidelined for Monday night's contest. Nick Barrett should see an uptick in defensive snaps in the absence of Eboigbe, whose next chance to play is Week 11 against the Jets on Nov. 22.

injuries.longComment: inactive

injuries.shortComment: inactive
injuries.longComment: inactive

injuries.shortComment: inactive
injuries.longComment: inactive

injuries.shortComment: inactive
injuries.longComment: inactive

injuries.shortComment: Pipkins (knee) won't be available for Monday's game against the Ravens after the Chargers didn't activate him from injured reserve.
injuries.longComment: Pipkins has been sidelined since Week 1, but he had his 21-day practice window opened Thursday and was listed as questionable heading into Monday. Assuming he can continue practicing in Week 11 without issue, Pipkins could be activated ahead of the Chargers' next game Nov. 22 versus the Jets. Once reinstated, Pipkins could settle back in as the team's starting left guard.

injuries.shortComment: Taylor (ankle) was placed on injured reserve Monday.
injuries.longComment: Taylor is battling an ankle injury and was ruled out for the Week 10 meeting with Baltimore. Now on injured reserve, he will be required to miss at least four games before being eligible to return.

injuries.shortComment: The Chargers activated Perryman (pectoral) from the reserve/injured list ahead of Monday's game versus Baltimore.
injuries.longComment: Perryman is finally cleared to suit up after missing the entire season due to a pec issue. While his return is good news for the Chargers, it may take him a game or two to get back to full speed.

injuries.shortComment: The Chargers activated Njoku (fibula) from injured reserve ahead of Monday's game against the Ravens.
injuries.longComment: After completing his second week of practice upon being designated for return from IR on Nov. 4, Njoku had been listed as questionable heading into Monday. The Chargers ultimately came away encouraged enough by how Njoku looked during the week of practice to activate him, giving the team a third option at tight end for Monday's game. Due to his blocking prowess, Charlie Kolar likely will lead the position group in snaps Monday, but Njoku could usurp Oronde Gadsden as the Chargers' top pass-catching tight end as he takes the field for the first time since Week 2.

injuries.shortComment: Leonard (concussion) does not have a designation for Monday's matchup against Baltimore.
injuries.longComment: Leonard suffered a concussion at some point between the Chargers' Week 6 loss to Kansas City and the team's Week 7 bye. He missed the club's past two contests but has now passed through the NFL's concussion protocol and has been cleared to return to game action. Leonard should assume a rotational role in Los Angeles' secondary.

injuries.shortComment: Mitchell (hip) does not carry an injury designation into Monday's game against the Ravens.
injuries.longComment: Mitchell's practice reps were limited by a hip injury, but he's been officially cleared to play Monday against the team he spent three seasons with from 2023 to 2025. He turned 10 touches into 67 yards during the Chargers' Week 9 loss to the Texans, and Mitchell will continue to operate in a rotational role in the backfield alongside Omarion Hampton and Kimani Vidal.

injuries.shortComment: Hart (ankle) practiced in full Friday.
injuries.longComment: Hart upgraded to full participation in Friday's practice after being limited during Thursday's session. The cornerback therefore should be set to suit up for Monday night's contest against the Ravens.

injuries.shortComment: Harris (calf) was a full participant in Friday's practice.
injuries.longComment: After being limited the day before, Harris erased any doubt about his availability for Monday's game at Baltimore. He saw a team-high seven targets on a 79 percent route share last week, catching three passes for a mere six yards in the 44-22 loss to Houston. Harris' volume projection for Week 10 partially depends on Ladd McConkey (back), who didn't play any snaps last week and didn't practice Thursday or Friday.

injuries.shortComment: Herbert (finger) doesn't appear on the the Chargers' injury report ahead of Monday night's game against the Ravens.
injuries.longComment: Chargers coach Jim Harbaugh previously noted that the QB "should be good to go" for Week 10 action after imaging on Herbert's injured left middle finger came back negative for a fracture, per ESPN.com. The fact that Herbert isn't listed in any way on the team's first injury report this week aligns with that and paves the way for him to continue to helm the offense for 0-8 Los Angeles versus Baltimore.

injuries.shortComment: Henley remains with the Chargers, as the Broncos have backed out of trading for the linebacker, Jeff Legwold of ESPN.com reports.
injuries.longComment: A trade involving Henley was agreed to Tuesday pending a physical, but the Broncos apparently found a red flag concerning his knee during that physical. Denver offered an updated trade to the Chargers with different draft compensation than the originally agreed upon 2027 fourth-round pick and 2028 fifth-round pick, but the two sides were unable to agree on an updated framework, so Henley will ultimately remain with the Chargers. Henley has not missed a game this season, so the concern Denver discovered on his physical isn't expected to impact his availability for Monday's game against the Ravens.

injuries.shortComment: Lambert-Smith registered one catch (on four targets) for 50 yards in Sunday's loss to Houston.
injuries.longComment: Lambert-Smith wasn't exactly prolific in spite of logging a hearty 40 offensive snaps, but he made his one catch count, hauling in a 50-yard reception in the third quarter. However, the woeful Chargers turned the ball over on a fumble two plays later. Lambert-Smith has spent much of the season on IR and has had an inconsistent role when suiting up, but he was deployed pretty heavily Sunday because Ladd McConkey couldn't play due to back spasms. If McConkey is also sidelined next Monday in Baltimore, Lambert-Smith could again be a fairly big part of Los Angeles' air attack.

injuries.shortComment: Vidal rushed seven times for 30 yards in Sunday's 44-22 loss to the Texans. He added one catch for six yards on three targets.
injuries.longComment: The Chargers continue to use a three-man backfield, an unfriendly fantasy situation and one to avoid when making lineup decisions each week. Vidal has been productive when he does get touches, rushing 36 times for 162 yards (4.5 YPC) and one touchdown across eight games. He's also caught 10 passes for 56 yards and an additional score.

injuries.shortComment: Kolar brought in all three of his targets for 31 yards in a 44-22 loss to the Texans on Sunday.
injuries.longComment: Kolar has recorded three catches in four of his last five outings, although he's cracked 30-plus receiving yards in just two of those contests. The Chargers average a season-low 15.1 points per game, and their 201.9 receiving yards per game is ninth-fewest in the NFL, making pass catchers like Kolar hard to rely on for sustained production. The 0-8 Chargers will look to capture their first win of the season in Week 10 against the Ravens on Monday Night Football.

injuries.shortComment: Dicker went 3-for-3 on field-goal attempts and made his only PAT during Sunday's 44-22 loss to Houston.
injuries.longComment: Dicker was able to make multiple field-goal tries for the third straight game and fifth time this season. The kicker did all his damage in the first half, converting field goals from 52, 33 and 43 yards before the break. Dicker has now gone 15-for-17 on field-goal attempts, including 1-for-2 from 50-plus yards, over eight contests so far during the 2026 campaign.

injuries.shortComment: McManus made both of his field-goal attempts and all four PATs in the Rams' 34-6 win over the Cardinals on Sunday.
injuries.longComment: McManus' Sunday performance extends his perfect streak with a Rams special teams unit that desperately needed consistency at kicker. McManus is now 5-for-5 on field-goal attempts and 14-for-14 on PATs after five regular-season contests as a Ram in 2026.

injuries.shortComment: Higbee caught three of four targets for 17 yards and a touchdown during the Rams' 34-6 win over the Cardinals on Sunday.
injuries.longComment: Higbee's third and final catch of Sunday's game came late in the second quarter, with the veteran tight end connecting with Matthew Stafford for a five-yard touchdown to give the Rams a 10-6 lead. It was the second touchdown of the season for Higbee, with his first taking place in Week 3 against the Broncos. He's been held to three catches or fewer in each of his last four games, although he's been on the field for at least 50 offensive snaps in three of those contests. The Rams are on bye for Week 11, and Higbee's limited target share will take a hit if Davante Adams (hamstring) is activated from injured reserve ahead of Week 12 against the Packers on Wednesday, Nov. 25.

injuries.shortComment: Parkinson caught both of his targets for 11 yards during the Rams' 34-6 win over the Cardinals on Sunday.
injuries.longComment: Parkinson was able to shed an injury designation for Sunday's game after having his practice reps limited during Week 10 prep due to a lingering rib injury. His second catch of the contest went for 10 yards early in the third quarter and set the Rams up on the 1-yard line, with Blake Corum finding the end zone on the next play. Parkinson was on the field for 53 of the Rams' 76 offensive snaps (69.7 percent), and fellow tight ends Davis Allen (52) and Tyler Higbee (51) were not far behind. The Rams are committed to using their 13-man personnel, although the game plan could be slightly tweaked after the Week 11 bye if wide receiver Davante Adams (hamstring) is activated from injured reserve ahead of Week 12 against the Packers on Wednesday, Nov. 25. Parkinson has caught 20 passes (on 25 targets) for 127 yards and a touchdown through eight regular-season games.

injuries.shortComment: McMahon was placed on injured reserve Monday due to a partially torn patella tear that he suffered during the Rams' 34-6 win over the Cardinals on Sunday, Gary Klein of the Los Angeles Times reports.
injuries.longComment: A stint on injured reserve requires a player to miss at least the next four games. That means the earliest that McMahon can return is Week 16 against the Seahawks on Christmas day, but given the severity of the injury, it wouldn't be surprising if the third-year center was sidelined beyond that window. Coleman Shelton is expected to miss four-to-six weeks due to a hamstring injury, so Beaux Limmer and David Quessenberry are currently the next options at center for the Rams, who are on a bye for Week 11 before facing the Packers in Week 12 on Wednesday, Nov. 25.

injuries.shortComment: Shelton (hamstring) is set to miss several weeks due to injury, Greg Beacham of the Associated Press reports.
injuries.longComment: The starting center is set to miss 4-6 weeks with a hamstring injury. Shelton will likely be placed on injured reserve while he recovers. Dylan McMahon (knee, IR) also sustained an injury in the Rams' Week 10 win over the Cardinals, leaving Beaux Limmer to finish out the contest at center and likely with the new starting role for the foreseeable future.

injuries.shortComment: out
injuries.longComment: out

injuries.shortComment: Smith caught both of his targets for 40 yards and a touchdown in Sunday's 34-6 win over the Cardinals.
injuries.longComment: With the Rams down both Puka Nacua (knee/toe) and Davante Adams (hamstring) for the first time this season, Smith operated as the fourth receiver against Arizona, playing nine of 76 offensive snaps. His 22-yard touchdown in the second quarter was the first of Smith's career. Based on his small amount of playing time and routes run, Smith's 12-point PPR day isn't worth chasing in fantasy.

injuries.shortComment: Mumpfield brought in three of four targets for 81 yards in the Rams' 34-6 win over the Cardinals on Sunday.
injuries.longComment: With Puka Nacua (knee/toe) and Davante Adams (hamstring) on injured reserve, Mumpfield operated as the de facto No. 1 receiver for Matthew Stafford. Mumpfield met the moment with a team-high receiving yardage total that more than doubled that of the next-closest pass catcher, Xavier Smith (40 yards). The 2025 seventh-round pick has now cleared the 80-yard mark twice this season, but Mumpfield could slide down to the No. 2 role in a Week 12 Thanksgiving Eve home matchup against the Packers on Nov. 25 if Adams is able to finish his recovery over the upcoming Week 11 bye.

injuries.shortComment: Stafford completed 18 of 26 passes for 249 yards with three touchdowns and one interception and rushed twice for minus-2 yards in the Rams' 34-6 win over the Cardinals on Sunday.
injuries.longComment: Stafford didn't let the fact he was without top wideouts Puka Nacua (IR, knee/toe) and Davante Adams (IR, hamstring) deter him from a very fantasy-friendly performance, as the reigning NFL MVP tossed at least three TD passes for the fourth time this season. Stafford connected with the unlikely trio of Tyler Higbee (five yards), Xavier Smith (22 yards) and Davis Allen (19 yards) for his scoring strikes, and the quarterback's 9.6 yards per attempt was his second-highest figure of the season. Stafford, who'll have a chance to further build chemistry with his current wideouts during the Week 11 bye, could have Adams back for a Week 12 Thanksgiving Eve matchup against the Packers on Nov. 25, as reports earlier Sunday indicated the talented wideout is targeting that game for his return.

injuries.shortComment: Williams rushed 12 times for 23 yards and brought in two of five targets for nine yards in the Rams' 34-6 win over the Cardinals on Sunday.
injuries.longComment: Williams was held well under 4.0 yards per carry for the third consecutive game, but Sunday's performance was particularly alarming in that he averaged a minuscule 1.9 yards per carry. In contrast, Blake Corum (17-100-1) and Ronnie Rivers (15-81-0, albeit in garbage time) both had multiple productive runs on the way to efficient afternoons, making Williams' struggles stand out all the more. With Corum particularly playing well in the last several weeks, Williams could be relegated to a clear complementary role in a Week 12 Thanksgiving Eve home showdown with the Packers on Nov. 25, following a Week 11 bye.

injuries.shortComment: Corum rushed 17 times for 100 yards and a touchdown and brought in three of four targets for 19 yards in the Rams' 34-6 win over the Cardinals on Sunday.
injuries.longComment: Corum was far more productive than backfield mate Kyren Williams, who he outpaced by five carries and 77 rushing yards. It was the fourth straight game with double-digit rush attempts and a touchdown for Corum, with Sunday's score coming from one yard out early in the third quarter. He has at least 73 rushing yards in three of the last four contests, and it remains to be seen if Sunday's division of labor will have any sticking power when Los Angeles returns to action following a Week 11 bye in a Week 12 home Thanksgiving Eve matchup against the Packers on Nov. 25.

injuries.shortComment: Cardona (ankle) is inactive for Sunday's game against Arizona.
injuries.longComment: Cardona will end up missing a third consecutive game while recovering from an ankle injury, and his next chance to play is Week 12 against the Packers on Wednesday, Nov. 25. Jake McQuaide will once again serve as the Rams' long snapper.

injuries.shortComment: McDuffie (back) is active for Sunday's game against the Cardinals.
injuries.longComment: McDuffie missed three of the Rams' last four games due to a persistent back injury. The cornerback is all set to suit up for Sunday's game, as he and Kam Curl return to reinforce the Rams' secondary in time for a divisional matchup with the Cardinals' rookie quarterback Carson Beck.

injuries.shortComment: Curl (toe) is active for Sunday's game against the Cardinals.
injuries.longComment: Curl's sole limited practice session Friday was enough to cement his availability for Sunday's contest. The strong safety has started every contest for the Rams in 2026, playing 100 percent of the defensive snaps in six of the Rams' nine games.

injuries.shortComment: Allen (oblique) is active for Sunday's game against the Cardinals.
injuries.longComment: Allen has recovered enough from the oblique injury he suffered during the Rams' Week 9 win over the Commanders to suit up for Week 10. The No. 3 tight end is a key part of the Rams' 13-personnel offense, and he should continue seeing a significant share of offensive snaps for the team.

injuries.shortComment: Simpson (coach's decision) is inactive but will serve as the Rams' emergency third quarterback in Sunday's game against the Cardinals.
injuries.longComment: Simpson continues to be inactive behind Matthew Stafford and Stetson Bennett. The quarterback will only enter the game if both Stafford and Bennett must exit due to injury, illness or ejection.

injuries.shortComment: Garrett (knee) is listed as active Sunday at Arizona, Adam Grosbard of The Orange County Register reports.
injuries.longComment: Garrett was listed as limited on the Rams' first two Week 10 practice reports due to a knee injury and then got a veteran's rest day Friday, heading into the weekend listed as questionable. Head coach Sean McVay told Sarah Barshop of ESPN.com on Friday that Garrett is expected to play Sunday, which now has been confirmed. Garrett will be looking to have a similar impact to the 3.0-sack day he had in Week 9 against the Commanders.

injuries.shortComment: According to Ian Rapoport of NFL Network and ESPN,  Adams (hamstring) is believed to be targeting a return to action Nov. 25 against the Packers.
injuries.longComment: Rapoport also noted Sunday that Adams' fellow WR Puka Nacua (knee/toe) has an estimated return in the mid-December range. For now, Konata Mumpfield and Tutu Atwell are in line to lead the WR corps of the Rams (who are on bye in Week 11), with CJ Daniels, Xavier Smith and Brennan Presley also on hand.

injuries.shortComment: Nacua (knee/toe) has an expected return date of "mid-December," Ian Rapoport of NFL Network reports.
injuries.longComment: After the Rams placed Nacua on injured reserve Thursday, Nacua must miss at least four games, which means his earliest return date is Sunday, Dec. 20 against the Cowboys. Considering the timeline given in Rapoport's report, Nacua thus may miss only the minimum number of contests while on IR after suffering PCL and MCL sprains and also a turf-toe injury last Sunday at Washington. With Davante Adams (hamstring) out at least one more outing, L.A. is rolling with a receiving corps of Konata Mumpfield, Tutu Atwell, CJ Daniels, Xavier Smith and Brennan Presley in Week 10.

injuries.shortComment: Head coach Sean McVay said Friday that Daniels "will get an opportunity to play more snaps moving forward," Stu Jackson of the Rams' official site reports.
injuries.longComment: Daniels has seen minimal playing time this season, but he'll be thrust into a more prominent role offensively due to both Puka Nacua (knee/toe) and Davante Adams (hamstring) being on injured reserve. As such, Daniels -- a sixth-round selection of the Rams in the 2026 NFL Draft -- is slated to serve as the team's WR3 behind Konata Mumpfield and Tutu Atwell for Sunday's game against the Cardinals, with Xavier Smith and Brennan Presley also in the mix for snaps on offense. During his final college season in Miami, Daniels recorded 50 catches for 557 yards and seven touchdowns across 13 games.

injuries.shortComment: Landman recorded seven tackles (three solo), one pass breakup and a forced fumble in Sunday's 20-13 win over the Commanders.
injuries.longComment: Much like last season, when Landman set a career high with 132 tackles across 17 starts, he's racking up the tackles through eight games in 2026. The middle linebacker is up to 66 tackles (37 solo), three forced fumbles and two pass breakups on 86 percent of the defensive snaps. Interestingly, Landman's snaps have been cut some since he returned from a concussion in Week 8. Over the last two weeks, he's played less than 70 percent of the defensive snaps after playing more than 90 percent across Weeks 1 through 6.

injuries.shortComment: Biggers will undergo a season-ending knee surgery in the near future, Ian Rapoport of NFL Network reports.
injuries.longComment: Biggers suffered a meniscus injury in the first quarter of Sunday's 24-22 loss to the Colts, and he will now be forced to miss the team's final eight games of the regular season. In his absence, Jordan Phillips (arm) and Kenneth Grant will likely operate as the team's primary defensive tackles moving forward.

injuries.shortComment: Wright turned three carries into minus-2 yards, caught both of his targets for 17 yards and returned four kickoffs for 88 yards during the Dolphins' 24-22 loss to the Colts on Sunday.
injuries.longComment: Wright's first touch on offense came midway through the second quarter and resulted in a carry for minus-3 yards, although he did connect with Kyle McCord for a 16-yard catch late in the third. Wright was on the field for 12 of the Dolphins' 69 offensive snaps (17.4 percent), which was far behind lead back Ollie Gordon (49 snaps). Wright is averaging only 1.6 YPC on 25 rushes through seven regular-season games, and most of his on-field impact has come on special teams as a returner on kickoffs. The Dolphins will stay on the road for Week 11 against the Bills on Nov. 22.

injuries.shortComment: Allen turned his lone carry into zero yards and hauled in his lone target for minus-4 yards during the Dolphins' 24-22 loss to the Colts on Sunday.
injuries.longComment: Allen found the ball on both of his offensive snaps during Sunday's loss, although he ended up losing four yards on his only catch of the game early in the second quarter. He's well behind Ollie Gordon and Jaylen Wright on the running back depth chart, and most of Allen's playing time in Week 11 against the Bills on Nov. 22, likely will come on special teams.

injuries.shortComment: Phillips underwent further tests Monday on the arm he injured in Sunday's 24-22 loss to the Colts, Barry Jackson of the Miami Herald reports.
injuries.longComment: Phillips was seen wearing an arm sling after Sunday's loss in Indianapolis. Dolphins head coach Jeff Hafley said the team has "concerns" about the injury but had no more updates to add. Keith Cooper and Kenneth Grant will likely see more snaps should Phillips miss time.

injuries.shortComment: Head coach Jeff Hafley said Monday that Willis (groin/core) has not undergone surgery and that the Dolphins are still determining if a procedure is needed, David Furones of the South Florida Sun Sentinel reports.
injuries.longComment: Per Barry Jackson of the Miami Herald, Hafley noted on that subject Monday, "We will see how he feels. If he needs surgery, he will have surgery," while adding that if the QB does undergo a procedure, it wouldn't "necessarily" be season ending. In any case, the earliest Willis can come off IR is Week 14, with Kyle McCord and Brady Cook currently available to handle Miami's signal-caller duties.

injuries.shortComment: Traore went without a target while playing six of the Dolphins' 69 snaps on offense in Sunday's 24-22 loss to the Colts.
injuries.longComment: Meanwhile, Traore tied a season-high with 23 snaps on special teams, where he continues to receive the bulk of his playing time. The reserve tight end has played in all nine of the Dolphins' games to date but has gone without a reception while being targeted once across 39 total snaps on offense.

injuries.shortComment: Dulcich failed to haul in either of his two targets while logging 42 of 69 offensive snaps in the Dolphins' 24-22 loss to the Colts on Sunday.
injuries.longComment: Second-year signal-caller Kyle McCord threw for 209 yards on 32 attempts in his first NFL start, but he couldn't forge much of a connection with Dulcich, who was held without a catch for the second time this season. With Malik Willis (core) out for at least three more contests while on injured reserve, Dulcich will have more time to build a rapport with McCord, but the tight end was far from a reliable fantasy option even when Willis was directing the offense. Despite playing more than 50 percent of the offensive snaps in each of the Dolphins' nine games, Dulcich has been limited to 24 receptions for 270 yards and has yet to find the end zone.

injuries.shortComment: Tolbert caught both of his targets for 49 yards and a touchdown in Sunday's 24-22 loss to the Colts.
injuries.longComment: The wideout was active for just the fifth time in nine games this season and played 11 of 69 offensive snaps. He ran only five routes and caught a 34-yard touchdown from fellow receiver Malik Washington on a trick play early in the second quarter. Tolbert has no fantasy appeal moving forward, as he has just four catches for 79 yards on six targets this season.

injuries.shortComment: Washington secured all three targets for 50 yards, threw a 34-yard touchdown on his one pass attempt and returned four punts for 36 yards in the Dolphins' 24-22 loss to the Colts on Sunday.
injuries.longComment: Washington finished second in receiving yards for the Dolphins and also was partly responsible for the team's one score through the air, uncorking a well-thrown 34-yard strike to Jalen Tolbert on a trick play. Washington also continued to produce in his returner role, and he's now up to 812 all-purpose yards through nine games heading into a Week 11 road matchup against the Bills next Sunday.

injuries.shortComment: Douglas brought in three of eight targets for 71 yards in the Dolphins' 24-22 loss to the Colts on Sunday.
injuries.longComment: Douglas posted a team-high yardage total with a big hand from his game-long 38-yard grab. Douglas garnered plenty of first-time starter Kyle McCord's attention as evidenced by the receiver's team-high target tally, and he's now hit or exceeded the 70-yard mark in three of the past four games. The 2026 third-round pick will look to carry over the momentum into a tough Week 11 road matchup against the Bills next Sunday.

injuries.shortComment: McCord completed 17 of 32 passes for 209 yards with no touchdowns or interceptions and rushed twice for four yards and a touchdown in the Dolphins' 24-22 loss to the Colts on Sunday. He also lost a fumble that was returned for a touchdown.
injuries.longComment: Drawing his first career start as a result of Malik Willis having gone on injured reserve with an abdomen injury earlier in the week, McCord acquitted himself well overall in a favorable matchup. The 2025 sixth-round pick of the Eagles spread the ball around to nine different targets, and he had a statement three-yard touchdown run on the first play of the fourth quarter when he powered through a pair of defenders and broke the plane despite having his facemask pulled. McCord's one turnover was very costly, however, as it was recovered on the Dolphins' six-yard line and returned for a short touchdown. McCord should only get more comfortable by following up Sunday's solid showing with another week of practice, but he'll draw a tough Week 11 road matchup against the Bills next Sunday.

injuries.shortComment: Gordon rushed 20 times for 76 and brought in four of five targets for 39 yards in the Dolphins' 24-22 loss to the Colts on Sunday.
injuries.longComment: Filling his customary workhorse role in Miami's ground attack, Gordon handled all but four of the Dolphins' running back carries while finishing with a team-high reception total. The second-year back eclipsed 75 rushing yards for the fourth time in six games in the process, and Gordon's catch and receiving yardage totals were also season highs. Gordon should remain in a high-volume role in a Week 11 road matchup against the Bills next Sunday.

injuries.shortComment: Meyer (stinger) is questionable to return to Sunday's matchup against Indianapolis.
injuries.longComment: Meyer started Sunday in place of Aaron Brewer, who was unable to suit up due to a concussion. With Meyer now at least temporarily sidelined, Jarrett Kingston has taken over at center for Miami.

injuries.shortComment: Baker (knee) was not activated from the reserve/PUP list ahead of Sunday's clash against Indianapolis.
injuries.longComment: Baker was designated to return to practice Wednesday, but he isn't yet ready for game action. The veteran cornerback hasn't yet played for Miami after signing a one-year contract to join the organization last March. Baker's next chance to suit up will be Sunday, Nov. 22, in Buffalo.

injuries.shortComment: Kacmarek (quadriceps) does not have any injury designation ahead of Sunday's game against the Colts, David Furones of the South Florida Sun Sentinel reports.
injuries.longComment: Kacmarek upgraded his practice participation in each Week 10 prep session. The tight end went from a non-participant Wednesday to a full participant by Friday's session. Kacmarek is all set to suit up as the No. 2 tight end behind Greg Dulcich for Sunday's game against the Colts.

injuries.shortComment: Brooks recorded 12 tackles (four solo) during Sunday's 19-9 loss versus the Lions.
injuries.longComment: Brooks played all 59 of the Dolphins' defensive snaps in Week 9, and he compiled a double-digit tackle total for the fourth time in his last six games. He's easily on pace for his sixth consecutive 100-tackle season going into a Week 10 matchup at Indianapolis.

injuries.shortComment: Rodriguez recorded 10 tackles (seven solo) including 1.0 sacks during Sunday's 19-9 loss versus the Lions.
injuries.longComment: Rodriguez and the entire Dolphins defense performed well against a strong Detroit offense in Week 9, especially against the run. Rodriguez also recorded the first sack of his pro career late in the first quarter, pushing quarterback Jared Goff out of bounds for no gain. He ranks seventh in the NFL in total tackles on the season going into a Week 10 tilt at Indianapolis.

injuries.shortComment: Reichard made all three of his field-goal attempts and all three PATs in the Vikings' 30-10 win over the Packers on Sunday.
injuries.longComment: All three of Reichard's field goals came from fewer than 40 yards out in the contest. The return of Kirk Cousins allowed Minnesota's offense to surge to its highest touchdown total since Week 1, the team's first bout against the Packers. Reichard is now 23-for-25 on field-goal attempts and remains perfect at 13-for-13 on PATs over nine regular-season games in 2026.

injuries.shortComment: Price is set for an increase in offensive workload with Jordan Addison (thumb) sidelined, Kevin Seifert of ESPN.com reports.
injuries.longComment: Price reeled in a season-high four passes for 49 yards and a score during Sunday's 30-10 win over the Packers. The wideout was operating in a more prominent offensive role for the second week in a row with Jauan Jennings (calf) sidelined, and fellow wide receiver Jordan Addison (thumb) was unable to play as well. Addison is now expected to undergo thumb surgery, opening the door for Price to operate in an elevated position on Minnesota's offense for the time being.

injuries.shortComment: Felton is on track to operate in a more prominent role in Week 11 versus the 49ers, Kevin Seifert of ESPN.com reports.
injuries.longComment: Felton drew a start in Sunday's 30-10 win over the Packers, reeling in a season-high three of five targets for 33 yards over 56 offensive snaps. The wide receiver stepped into a starting role as a result of Jordan Addison (thumb) being sidelined, and Addison is now reportedly set to undergo surgery to address his injury, opening the door for more opportunities for Felton moving forward.

injuries.shortComment: Van Ginkel (quadriceps) is expected to practice ahead of a Week 11 road matchup against the 49ers, Kevin Seifert of ESPN.com reported Monday.
injuries.longComment: Van Ginkel sustained a quad injury late in Sunday's game against Green Bay. The 31-year-old has yet to miss a regular-season game in 2026, recording 28 tackles (16 solo), including 8.5 sacks, and one interception in nine contests.

injuries.shortComment: Vikings head coach Kevin O'Connell said Monday that Addison will require surgery on his thumb and will miss a few weeks, Alec Lewis of The Athletic reports.
injuries.longComment: O'Connell indicated that Addison will be a candidate for injured reserve, though if he does end up being deactivated, the Vikings anticipate that the wideout would be able to return after sitting out the minimum four games. Addison injured his thumb at Friday's practice and subsequently was inactive for Sunday's 30-10 win over Green Bay. For as long as Addison is sidelined, Jauan Jennings (calf), Myles Price and Tai Felton will be the options to see added reps behind No. 1 receiver Justin Jefferson.

injuries.shortComment: Coach Kevin O'Connell said Monday that the Vikings expect Hockenson (wrist/chest) to make progress ahead of Sunday's game against the 49ers, Alec Lewis of The Athletic reports.
injuries.longComment: Hockenson was inactive for Sunday's 30-10 win over the Packers, but it sounds like the tight end has a chance to return to practice after logging DNPs last week. In Hockenson's absence versus Green Bay in Week 10, fellow TE Gavin Bartholomew caught three of his four targets for 36 yards and a TD.

injuries.shortComment: Bartholomew caught three of four targets for 36 yards and a touchdown in Sunday's 30-10 win over the Packers.
injuries.longComment: With T.J. Hockenson (wrist) inactive, Bartholomew played 53 of 69 offensive snaps against Green Bay and caught the second of Kirk Cousins' two touchdowns, scoring from 20 yards out in the fourth quarter to give Minnesota a comfortable 27-10 lead. While Ben Yurosek got the start, Bartholomew played 13 more snaps and out-targeted Yurosek four to one. Cousins has an affinity for throwing to his tight ends, so Bartholomew will be on the fantasy radar if Hockenson needs to miss more time.

injuries.shortComment: Jones carried the ball 11 times for 47 yards and a touchdown and caught his only target for eight yards in Sunday's 30-10 win over the Packers.
injuries.longComment: Jordan Mason led the Vikings with 59 rushing yards, but Jones had the more productive afternoon as he scored his first TD since Week 5 on a one-yard plunge in the second quarter. Jones' upside will remain limited while working in a timeshare with Mason, but he's still got some utility heading into a Week 11 clash with the 49ers.

injuries.shortComment: Mason carried the ball 16 times for 59 yards and failed to catch his only target in Sunday's 30-10 win over the Packers.
injuries.longComment: The fifth-year RB led the Vikings in rushing yards, but Aaron Jones was the more productive player in the backfield, gaining 55 scrimmage yards on 12 touches and scoring on a one-yard plunge in the second quarter. Mason has yet to get into the end zone in four games since returning from a thumb injury, piecing together 182 rushing yards on 4.0 yards per carry while working in a timeshare with Jones. He could break that drought in Week 11 in a potential revenge game against the 49ers.

injuries.shortComment: Cousins completed 21 of 31 passes for 207 yards and two touchdowns with one interception in Sunday's 30-10 win over the Packers. He added 11 rushing yards on three carries.
injuries.longComment: Brought back to Minnesota at the trade deadline to stabilize the offense, Cousins did exactly that, connecting with Myles Price for a 38-yard TD in the first quarter and Gavin Bartholomew on a 20-yard score in the fourth while guiding Justin Jefferson to season highs in catches and targets. The Vikings' passing game didn't need to over-extend itself, however, as the defense sacked Jordan Love eight times in another dominant performance. Cousins may need to find another gear in Week 11 against the 49ers, but he'll have another week of practice to re-familiarize himself with Kevin O'Connell's scheme first.

injuries.shortComment: Jefferson caught nine of 13 targets for 74 yards in Sunday's 30-10 win over the Packers.
injuries.longComment: In Kirk Cousins' return to the Vikings, Jefferson led the team in catches, targets and receiving yards, although Myles Price and Gavin Bartholomew were on the other end of the QB's two touchdown passes. The nine grabs and 13 targets were season highs for Jefferson, while the yardage total was his best showing since Week 5. Despite a disappointing 40-467-4 line on 64 targets through eight games, the star wideout's outlook for the rest of the year is pointed up heading into a Week 11 clash with the 49ers.

injuries.shortComment: Richter (foot) has been ruled out for the rest of Sunday's game against the Packers.
injuries.longComment: Richter injured his foot in the first quarter, and medical staff have determined that the injury is severe enough for the third-year linebacker to be sidelined for the rest of Sunday's contest. Richter's playing time this season has primarily come on special teams, and his availability for Week 11 against the 49ers on Nov. 22, is up in the air.

injuries.shortComment: Van Noy (calf) is active for Sunday's game against the Packers.
injuries.longComment: Van Noy tweaked his calf during the Vikings' Week 9 loss to the Bills. He earned the questionable tag for Week 10 after logging a limited practice Friday, and he was cleared by medical staff to play in Sunday's NFC North showdown. Van Noy has 15 tackles (nine solo), including 1.5 sacks, through eight regular-season games.

injuries.shortComment: Metellus (shoulder) is active for Sunday's game against the Packers.
injuries.longComment: Metellus was added to the Vikings' practice report Friday due to a shoulder issue, but the injury won't prevent the seventh-year pro from suiting up for Sunday's NFC North showdown. He has 58 tackles (29 solo), including 0.5 sacks, and four pass defenses through eight regular-season games.

injuries.shortComment: Wentz (ankle) doesn't have an injury designation for Sunday's game at Green Bay, but Kirk Cousins will be Minnesota's starting quarterback.
injuries.longComment: Kyler Murray (hamstring) is out for another week but may eventually replace Wentz as the No. 2 quarterback. Wentz's miserable performance against the Bills last week likely was a factor in the Vikings trading for Cousins.

injuries.shortComment: Wilson recorded nine tackles (three solo) in Monday night's 23-6 loss to the Bills.
injuries.longComment: The veteran linebacker has started all eight games this season, logging 94 percent of the defensive snaps for Minnesota. He's now up to 50 tackles (24 solo), including 3.0 sacks, seven QB hits and a pass breakup. He's been extremely productive under defensive coordinator Brian Flores over the last two seasons, recording 9.5 sacks as an off-bal linebacker across 25 regular-season games during that span.

injuries.shortComment: Dallas caught his only target for a two-yard gain in Monday's Week 9 loss to the Bills.
injuries.longComment: Dallas notched just eight offensive snaps but also contributed 19 snaps on special teams. The veteran running back went without a carry for the fourth time over Minnesota's past five games, indicating his lack of a role in the running game. Overall this season, Dallas has been a very small part of the Vikings' offense, recording four carries for 14 yards and five catches for 36 yards (on five targets) through eight contests.

injuries.shortComment: Mike Reiss of ESPN.com notes via ESPN's Adam Schefter that there are fears  DeVito's teammate, Drake Maye, may have sustained a fractured ankle during Week 10 action.
injuries.longComment: Regarding Maye's status going forward, head coach Mike Vrabel indicated that he'll wait for further information before estimating how long his starting QB might be out, but he also acknowledged he "wouldn't imagine him being available coming out of the (Week 11) bye," Phil Perry of NBC Sports Boston reports. As a result, DeVito is in a position to start Sunday, Nov. 29 against the Chargers and possibly beyond. That said, as NFL reporter Jordan Schultz suggests, New England is expected to explore the QB market in the coming days, be it through a practice squad addition or a veteran free agent such as Jimmy Garoppolo, who previously worked with  offensive coordinator Josh McDaniels.

injuries.shortComment: Patriots head coach Mike Vrabel said Monday that he didn't have a definitive diagnosis for the injury Maye (ankle) sustained in Sunday's 35-10 loss to the Lions in Munich, but indicated that the quarterback will miss time," Phil Perry of NBC Sports Boston reports.  "I wouldn't imagine him being available coming out of the [Week 11] bye," Vrabel said.
injuries.longComment: Adam Schefter of ESPN reported earlier Monday that the Patriots were concerned that Maye fractured his ankle Sunday. That diagnosis has yet to be confirmed, however, and Vrabel suggested that he'll avoid projecting a timeline for Maye until the quarterback returns from Germany to be further evaluated. At the very least, Maye can be expected to miss the Patriots' next game Nov. 29 against the Chargers. In the meantime, NFL reporter Jordan Schultz suggests that the team is expected to explore the quarterback market in the coming days, though top backup Tommy DeVito is currently next in line to start in place of Maye.

injuries.shortComment: Brown (hamstring) was spotted walking around with a limp in the locker room following Sunday's 35-10 loss to the Lions in Munich, Andrew Callahan of the Boston Herald reports.
injuries.longComment: Brown returned from a two-game absence caused by ankle and knee injuries to suit up Sunday. However, the veteran wideout sustained a hamstring injury while making a reception in the third quarter and wasn't able to return to the contest. Brown didn't speak to reporters following the loss, and head coach Mike Vrabel said the team would "see what the severity of that [injury] is" once the team returns to the United States. New England is on bye Week 11, but it's far from certain Brown will be able to suit up the next time the team plays Nov. 29 against the Chargers.

injuries.shortComment: Borregales made his sole field-goal attempt and one PAT in the Patriots' 35-10 loss to the Lions in Munich on Sunday.
injuries.longComment: Borregales made a 33-yard field goal on the first drive of the game. The kicker is now 11-for-13 on field-goal attempts and 24-for-25 on PATs through 10 regular-season games in 2026.

injuries.shortComment: Douglas caught one of three passes for four yards during the Patriots' 35-10 loss to the Lions on Sunday in Munich.
injuries.longComment: The Patriots' offense was effective on the first drive of the game, but that was where the good news ended for New England after Drake Maye was knocked out for the rest of the contest due to an ankle injury. Tommy DeVito took over under center, and the offense struggled to move down the field for the rest of the game. For Douglas, it was the third time this season that he was held to one catch, with the last instance taking place in Week 3 against the Jaguars. A.J. Brown -- who was cleared to return from a two-game absence due to knee and ankle injuries -- also picked up a hamstring injury during Sunday's game, so Douglas could be the New England's WR1 following the Week 11 bye. The Patriots' next game takes place in Week 12 against the Chargers on Sunday, Nov. 29.

injuries.shortComment: Henry caught two of three passes for 22 yards during the Patriots' 35-10 loss to the Lions on Sunday in Munich.
injuries.longComment: Both of Henry's catches of 10 and 12 yards came on the Patriots' first offensive drive of the game, which ended with a 33-yard field goal by Andy Borregales. Unfortunately for the Patriots, Drake Maye suffered an ankle injury on the play prior to the field goal and was unable to return, and the offense struggled to move down the field with backup Tommy DeVito under center. Maye will undergo more tests once the team has returned to home soil, but the good news for the Patriots is that they are on a bye for Week 11, so the third-year quarterback has more time to heal before New England's next game in Week 12 against the Chargers on Sunday, Nov. 29. Henry's two catches Sunday were his fewest since Week 3 against the Jaguars (one), and the veteran tight end has a 34-383-2 receiving line on 40 targets through 10 regular-season games.

injuries.shortComment: Hollins caught five of six targets for 48 yards in Sunday's 35-10 loss to the Lions in Munich.
injuries.longComment: In his second game back from a calf injury, Hollins led the Patriots in catches and receiving yards, but the entire offense was compromised when Drake Maye (ankle) was knocked out of the game early. A.J. Brown (hamstring) also didn't last long in his latest return to action. New England gets a bye in Week 11, giving the team's injured stars a chance to recover, so Hollins' role and usage may not become clear until after the break. Over six appearances this season, Hollins has produced a 23-293-1 line on 32 targets.

injuries.shortComment: Kiner carried the ball 10 times for 25 yards in Sunday's 35-10 loss to Detroit.
injuries.longComment: Rhamondre Stevenson was active despite dealing with a knee issue during the practice week, but the veteran back gained just four yards on six carries, and Kiner wound up leading the Patriots' backfield in both volume and yardage. The entire offense struggles after Drake Maye (ankle) was knocked out of the game early, however. New England gets a Week 11 bye, so Kiner's role and usage for a Week 12 clash with the Chargers likely won't become clear until the health of Stevenson and Maye come into focus after the break.

injuries.shortComment: Stevenson carried the ball six times for four yards and caught his only target for one yard in Sunday's 35-10 loss to the Lions in Munich.
injuries.longComment: The whole Patriots' offense struggled after Drake Maye (ankle) was knocked out of the game early, but Stevenson also didn't look to be in peak form after dealing with a knee issue during the practice week. Corey Kiner wound up leading the backfield with just 25 rushing yards on 10 totes. Stevenson will get a Week 11 bye to rest up, and if Maye's injury ends up sidelining him for an extended period, New England could lean heavily on its running game in Week 12 against the Chargers.

injuries.shortComment: Jones (cramps) is questionable to return to Sunday's game against the Lions in Munich.
injuries.longComment: Jones left the game during the fourth quarter, and given the score of the contest, the veteran linebacker is unlikely to return to Sunday's game. If that's the case, then Jones will finish with two tackles (one solo) and one QB hit.

injuries.shortComment: Spillane (illness) is questionable to return to Sunday's game against the Lions in Munich.
injuries.longComment: Spillane went to the locker room in the third quarter, and he's being evaluated by medical staff to determine whether he can return to Sunday's international game. Darius Muasau has taken over for Spillane at inside linebacker.

injuries.shortComment: Moses (knee) has returned to Sunday's game against the Lions in Munich, Mike Reiss of ESPN.com reports.
injuries.longComment: Moses went to the locker room in the first quarter to have his knee injury evaluated. He's been cleared by medical staff to return and is back in at right tackle, with backup Caleb Lomu now on the sidelines.

injuries.shortComment: Van Roten (hamstring) is active for Sunday's game against the Lions in Munich.
injuries.longComment: Van Roten will be available to make his season debut after spending the first nine weeks of the campaign on injured reserve due to the hamstring issue. He was able to practice throughout Week 10 prep, turning in a pair of a limited sessions Wednesday and Thursday before upgrading to full activity Friday, and the Patriots activated him Saturday. With Ben Brown (knee) and Walter Rouse (concussion) inactive for the Germany game, Van Roten will likely draw the start at left guard.

injuries.shortComment: Woods (hamstring) is active for Sunday's game versus the Lions in Munich.
injuries.longComment: Woods didn't suit up for a Week 9 loss to the Packers due to a hamstring injury, but he followed an LP/LP/FP practice regimen this week, which was enough to gain clearance to return to action. With Carlton Davis (knee) inactive Sunday, Woods is a good bet to enter the starting lineup at outside cornerback opposite Christian Gonzalez.

injuries.shortComment: Byard (chest) is active for Sunday's game against the Lions in Munich.
injuries.longComment: The veteran safety was listed as questionable heading into Sunday, but his ability to finish Week 10 prep with a full practice seemingly had him trending toward playing. He'll end up suiting up in Germany and isn't expected to face any limitations while he plays through the chest issue. Through New England's first nine games, Byard has compiled 43 tackles, three pass breakups and an interception.

injuries.shortComment: Gilliam (knee) is active for Sunday's game against the Lions in Munich.
injuries.longComment: Gilliam took a questionable tag into Sunday, but the Patriots' decision to activate him from injured reserve Saturday signaled that he was on track to play for the first time since Week 4. The fullback served almost exclusively as a blocker when he was healthy during the Patriots' first four games of the season, logging no carries and recording a four-yard reception on two targets.

injuries.shortComment: Henderson (illness) was placed on injured reserve Saturday, Mike Reiss of ESPN.com reports.
injuries.longComment: Henderson was already ruled out for Sunday's game against the Lions in Munich, and now that he's on IR, the second-year running back will be required to miss at least the next four games. Henderson's next opportunity to play is Week 15 against the Chiefs on Monday, Dec. 21, although there's no timetable for his return, as he is recovering from "an unexpected and unusual medical emergency involving a series of neurological symptoms." If Rhamondre Stevenson (knee) cannot play Sunday, then the Patriots' backfield will be led by Corey Kiner and Lan Larison.

injuries.shortComment: Gonzalez logged 10 tackles (nine solo) and one pass defense during the Patriots' 45-27 loss to the Packers in Week 9.
injuries.longComment: Gonzalez's 10 stops were a season high, but the larger concern was his poor performance in coverage. Per Pro Football Focus, Gonzalez was on coverage for 11 catches for 192 yards and two touchdowns, and quarterback Jordan Love had a 158.3 passing rating while targeting the fourth-year defensive back. It wasn't the performance that the Patriots were expecting after signing Gonzalez to a lucrative four-year, $135 million contract extension in September. Things won't get easier for him or the Patriots' secondary, as they travel to Munich for Week 10 against the Lions, whose offense ranks fourth in the NFL in yards per game (379.8).

injuries.shortComment: Fant failed to haul in his lone target during the Saints' 20-17 loss to the Panthers on Sunday.
injuries.longComment: Fant didn't connect with Tyler Shough on a short pass late in the first quarter, and that ended up being the only target for the veteran tight end. Fant has a 12-96-3 line on 19 targets through eight regular-season games, although he's logged one reception or zero in four of his last five outings. He doesn't have much fantasy appeal as the Saints' TE2 behind Juwan Johnson heading into Week 11 against the Bears on Nov. 22.

injuries.shortComment: Vele caught both of his targets for 14 yards during the Saints' 20-17 loss to the Panthers on Sunday.
injuries.longComment: Vele was on the field for 55 of the Saints' 63 offensive snaps, which was second most among wide receivers behind Chris Olave (56). Despite that playing time, Vele saw only two targets Sunday, although no other Saints pass catcher logged more than three receptions other than rookie first-rounder Jordyn Tyson, who finished with 11 catches on 13 targets for 80 yards. Vele has two receptions in each of his last two outings, and it appears his role in the Saints' passing offense has shrunk due to the return of Tyson. Vele will look to bounce back for Week 11 against the Bears on Nov. 22, and Chicago's defense ranks 15th in the NFL in fantasy points allowed to receivers per game.

injuries.shortComment: Smyth reverted to the Saints' practice squad Monday, per the NFL's transaction log.
injuries.longComment: For a second week in a row, Smyth operated as the Saints' kicker during the team's 20-17 loss to the Panthers on Sunday, when he made both of his extra-point tries and connected on a 55-yard field goal late in the fourth quarter. Daniel Carlson was released by New Orleans on Nov. 3, so Smyth likely will be elevated to the active roster for Week 11 against the Bears on Nov. 22.

injuries.shortComment: Head coach Kellen Moore said Monday that Richards will be sidelined for multiple weeks due to a knee injury that the latter sustained during the Saints' 20-17 loss to the Panthers on Sunday, Matthew Paras of The New Orleans Times-Picayune reports.
injuries.longComment: Richards injured his knee during the fourth quarter of Sunday's game and wasn't cleared by medical staff to return. The injury appears severe enough for him to warrant an extended period of time on the shelf, so Richards is a candidate to be placed on injured reserve. Mason Murphy will likely move into the starting spot at right tackle for as long as Richards is sidelined.
